learningObjective: Identify true properties of the FX Graph produced by TorchDynamo.

canonicalClaims.claim: The FX Graph is a Python-level IR of nodes with `op`, `target`, `args`, `kwargs` fields; after AOTAutograd it is functionalized over ATen ops. It is a DAG for a single traced pass; Python loops are unrolled or preserved via higher-order ops for control flow.
conditions: The trace succeeded without unrecoverable graph break.
nonImplications: Does not imply all Python constructs can be captured.
Does not imply FX and TorchScript IRs are the same.

misconceptions.claim: FX Graphs are machine code and not inspectable from Python.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FX Graphs are Python objects; `graph.print_tabular()` and iteration are standard.

misconceptions.claim: FX Graph and TorchScript IR are the same.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They are distinct representations with different capabilities.

misconceptions.claim: FX Graph does not contain mutating ops in any circumstance.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Pre-AOTAutograd traces may contain in-place ops; functionalization removes them for the compiled path.

misconceptions.claim: Python `for` loops in the source are always preserved as loop ops in FX.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Most for-loops over Python-side ranges are unrolled during tracing; only higher-order loop ops persist as such.

implementationFacts: FX node ops include: placeholder, call_function, call_method, call_module, get_attr, output
Post-AOTAutograd graphs are typically functional and normalized to ATen ops
performanceScenarios: Reading the FX graph is a standard debugging step for graph break / recompile / fusion issues.
